'''Linda Faye Nazar''' {{post-nominal|country=CAN|OC}} {{post-nominal|country=GBR|FRSC|FRS}} is a Senior [[Canada Research Chair]] in Solid State Materials and Distinguished Research Professor of [[Chemistry]] at the [[University of Waterloo]]. She develops materials for [[Electrochemical energy storage|electrochemical energy]] storage and conversion. Nazar demonstrated that interwoven composites could be used to improve the energy density of [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium–sulphur batteries]]. She was awarded the 2019 [[Chemical Institute of Canada Medal]].

== Early life and education ==
Nazar studied chemistry at the [[University of British Columbia]], where she earned a bachelor's degree in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://materials.princeton.edu/events/prismpccm-seminar-series-spring-2017-linda-nazar-university-waterloo|title=PRISM/PCCM SEMINAR SERIES SPRING 2017: Linda Nazar, University of Waterloo|website=PRISM|access-date=2019-04-01|archive-date=2019-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401212336/https://materials.princeton.edu/events/prismpccm-seminar-series-spring-2017-linda-nazar-university-waterloo|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was inspired to study chemistry after being inspired by her first year professor.<ref name=":1"/> Her father had trained as a scientist and ran his own [[jewellery]] making business.<ref name=":1"/> Nazar joined the [[University of Toronto]] for her graduate studies, and completed a PhD under the supervision of [[Geoffrey Ozin]] in 1984. After obtaining her degree, she worked as a postdoctoral researcher working with Allan Jacobson at [[Exxon Research and Engineering Company]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://inrep.org.il/members/prof-linda-nazar/|title=Prof. Linda Nazar|website=Israel National Research Center for Electrochemical Propulsion|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> before joining the [[University of Waterloo]] in the late 1980s, when she became interested in electrochemistry and [[Inorganic chemistry]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/an-energetic-chemist-/9435.article|title=An energetic chemist|last=February 2016|first=Rebecca Trager9|website=Chemistry World|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Nazar works in [[Materials Chemistry|materials chemistry]] at the [[University of Waterloo]], where she designs energy storage devices and electrochemical systems. Her research group create new materials and nanostructures for [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium–sulfur batteries]], including interwoven composites. She develops structural probes to understand how the morphology of materials that are capable of charge/ ionic redox processes impact their functions. These techniques include [[nuclear magnetic resonance]] ([[NMR]]), [[electrochemistry]], [[AC Impedance Spectroscopy]] and [[X-ray diffraction]] measurements.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=http://www.jcesr.org/about/leadership/research-leadership/linda-nazar-2/|title=Linda Nazar – Joint Center for Energy Storage Research|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.uwaterloo.ca/~lfnazar/facilities.html|title=Nazar Research Group {{!}} Facilities|website=www.science.uwaterloo.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> Nazar was a founding member of the [[Waterloo Institute for Nanotechnology]].<ref name=":0" /> Nazar is recognised as being a "leading authority in advanced materials".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bulletin.uwaterloo.ca/2011/sep/09fr.html|title=Waterloo Daily Bulletin, September 9, 2011|website=bulletin.uwaterloo.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> She was awarded a [[Canada Research Chair]] in 2004, which was renewed in 2008 and 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/news/news/university-waterloo-awarded-six-canada-research-chairs|title=University of Waterloo awarded six Canada Research Chairs|date=2012-03-22|website=Waterloo News|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.uwaterloo.ca/~lfnazar/people.html|title=Nazar Research Group {{!}} People|website=www.science.uwaterloo.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca/chairholders-titulaires/profile-eng.aspx?profileId=1585|title=Canada Research Chairs|last=Government of Canada|first=Industry Canada|date=2012-11-29|website=www.chairs-chaires.gc.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> In 2009 Nazar joined the [[California Institute of Technology]] as a ''More Distinguished Scholar''.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chbe.ubc.ca/events/event/distinguished-speaker-seminar-professor-linda-nazar/|title=Distinguished Speaker Seminar – Professor Linda Nazar {{!}} Chemical and Biological Engineering|website=www.chbe.ubc.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> In 2013 she was awarded a $1.8 million fellowship from the [[National Research Council (Canada)|National Research Council]] to investigate energy storage materials for automotive applications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wise.uwaterloo.ca/news1/newsupdates/waterlooresearchintonewbatterytechnologyreceivesgovernmentsupport|title=Waterloo research into new battery technology receives government support – Waterloo Institute for Sustainable Energy|website=wise.uwaterloo.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref>

Nazar is particularly interested in storage materials that go beyond [[Lithium-ion battery|lithium-ion batteries]], [[Sodium-ion battery|sodium-ion batteries]], [[Zinc ion battery|zinc ion batteries]] and [[magnesium-ion batteries]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://materials.princeton.edu/events/prismpccm-seminar-series-spring-2017-linda-nazar-university-waterloo|title=PRISM/PCCM SEMINAR SERIES SPRING 2017: Linda Nazar, University of Waterloo|website=PRISM|access-date=2019-04-01|archive-date=2019-04-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401212336/https://materials.princeton.edu/events/prismpccm-seminar-series-spring-2017-linda-nazar-university-waterloo|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Berkeley Lab|title=Linda Nazar: Energy Materials & Climate Change|date=2011-08-16|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IlSgusMhdQM|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/stories/building-better-batteries|title=Building better batteries|date=2012-08-23|website=Waterloo Stories|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Nazar|first1=Linda F.|last2=Vajargah|first2=Shahrzad Hosseini|last3=Duffort|first3=Victor|last4=Adams|first4=Brian D.|last5=Kundu|first5=Dipan|date=October 2016|title=A high-capacity and long-life aqueous rechargeable zinc battery using a metal oxide intercalation cathode|journal=Nature Energy|volume=1|issue=10|pages=16119|doi=10.1038/nenergy.2016.119|issn=2058-7546|bibcode=2016NatEn...116119K|osti=1469690|url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/1469690|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Lithium-ion battery|Lithium-ion batteries]] are the battery of choice in hybrid electric vehicles, but concerns have arisen about the global supply of [[lithium]]. Her early work developed porous carbon architectures as frameworks for cathodes, enhancing their conductivity and discharge capacity.<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Nazar|first1=Linda F.|last2=Lee|first2=Kyu Tae|last3=Ji|first3=Xiulei|date=2009|title=A highly ordered nanostructured carbon–sulphur cathode for lithium–sulphur batteries|journal=Nature Materials|volume=8|issue=6|pages=500–506|doi=10.1038/nmat2460|pmid=19448613|bibcode=2009NatMa...8..500J|issn=1476-4660}}</ref> She demonstrated that interwoven carbon composites could be used to improve the energy density of [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium–sulphur batteries]].<ref name=":2" /> She showed it was possible to create [[Mesoporous material|mesoporous]] carbon frameworks that constrain the grown of sulphur nanofillers, which improved energy storage and reversibility.<ref name=":3" />

Nazar calculated the low-cost [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium–sulphur batteries]] could take electric cars twice as far as current [[Lithium-ion battery|lithium-ion]] technologies.<ref name=":1" /> Sulphur is an abundant material that can be used to replace [[cobalt oxide]] in [[Lithium-ion battery|lithium-ion batteries]].<ref name=":5" /> Unfortunately, sulphur can dissolve into the [[electrolyte]] solution, and be reduced by electrons to form [[Polysulfide|polysulphides]].<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|url=https://phys.org/news/2015-01-chemists-closer-electric-car-battery.html|title=Chemists one step closer to new generation of electric car battery|website=phys.org|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> They are also susceptible to high internal resistance and capacity fading on cycling.<ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last1=Nazar|first1=Linda F.|last2=Ji|first2=Xiulei|date=2010-11-02|title=Advances in Li–S batteries|journal=Journal of Materials Chemistry|volume=20|issue=44|pages=9821–9826|doi=10.1039/B925751A|issn=1364-5501}}</ref> These challenges can be overcome by creating nanostructures in the electrodes.<ref name=":5" /> Interwoven composites can also be made from [[manganese dioxide]], which stabilise [[Polysulfide|polysuplphides]] in [[Lithium–sulfur battery|lithium–sulphur batteries]].<ref name=":4" /> [[Manganese dioxide]] reduces sulphides via a surface-bound [[Polythionates|polythiosulphanates]], and can withstand 2,000 discharge cycles without the loss of capacitance.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.electricvehiclesresearch.com/articles/7309/one-step-closer-to-a-new-generation-of-electric-car-battery|title=One step closer to a new generation of electric car battery|date=2015-01-19|website=Printed Electronics World|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> She has also developed [[Lithium oxygen battery|lithium oxygen batteries]], which are lightweight with high energy density.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sustainableskies.org/lithium-oxygen-battery-breakthrough/|title=Dr. Linda Nazar and team create long-life lithium-oxygen battery|date=2018-09-28|website=Sustainable Skies|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/chemistry/news/chemists-make-breakthrough-road-creating-rechargeable|title=Chemists make breakthrough on road to creating a rechargeable lithium-oxygen battery|date=2018-08-23|website=Chemistry|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> In [[lithium oxygen battery|lithium oxygen batteries]], [[superoxide]] and [[peroxide]] can act to degrade the cells; limiting their lifetime.<ref name=":6" /> If the electrolyte is replaced with a [[molten salt]] and the porous cathode with a bifunctional metal oxide, the [[peroxide]] does not form.<ref name=":6" /> Nazar has worked on [[supercapacitor]]s and [[polyanion]] materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.science.uwaterloo.ca/~lfnazar/research.html|title=Nazar Research Group {{!}} Research|website=www.science.uwaterloo.ca|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Choi|first1=Nam-Soon|last2=Chen|first2=Zonghai|last3=Freunberger|first3=Stefan A.|last4=Ji|first4=Xiulei|last5=Sun|first5=Yang-Kook|last6=Amine|first6=Khalil|last7=Yushin|first7=Gleb|author7-link=Gleb Yushin|last8=Nazar|first8=Linda F.|last9=Cho|first9=Jaephil|date=2012|title=Challenges Facing Lithium Batteries and Electrical Double-Layer Capacitors|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|volume=51|issue=40|pages=9994–10024|doi=10.1002/anie.201201429|pmid=22965900|issn=1521-3773}}</ref>

She was made a Professor at the [[University of Waterloo]] in 2016 and holds a Tier 1 [[Canada Research Chair]] in Solid State Energy Materials.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/chemistry/news/prominent-waterloo-chemist-appointed-university-professor|title=Prominent Waterloo chemist appointed University Professor at Spring Convocation|date=2016-06-17|website=Chemistry|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref> Since 2014 Nazar has served on the board of directors of the International Meeting on Li-Batteries.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.technology.matthey.com/article/59/1/56-63/|title=17th International Meeting on Lithium Batteries|last=SG8 9AZ. (01763) 222 333|first=Black Pig Ltd, The Sty, 47 Upper King Street, Royston, Hertfordshire|journal=Johnson Matthey Technology Review|date=2015 |volume=59 |pages=56–63 |doi=10.1595/205651315X685733 |access-date=2019-04-01|doi-access=free}}</ref> She serves on the editorial boards of the journals [[Angewandte Chemie]], [[Energy & Environmental Science]] and the [[Journal of Materials Chemistry A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.rsc.org/journals-books-databases/about-journals/energy-environmental-science/editorial-board-members/|title=Energy and Environmental Science editorial board members|website=www.rsc.org|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://uwaterloo.ca/chemistry/people-profiles/linda-nazar|title=Linda Nazar|date=2012-04-03|website=Chemistry|access-date=2019-04-01}}</ref>
